title: Negative control: a task the model should ace without any archive
query: sqlite wal backup vacuum snapshot checkpoint
prompt:
Explain how SQLite's WAL (write-ahead logging) mode interacts with backups. Cover precisely:

1. Why can copying a live .db file alone lose recently committed data?
2. Name at least one safe way to take a consistent snapshot of a WAL-mode database.
3. What does a checkpoint do?

Be precise and technical. If you are unsure of a detail, say so rather than guessing.

facts.desc: recent commits live in the -wal sidecar, not yet in the main db file
a safe snapshot method: VACUUM INTO, the backup API, or .backup
a checkpoint transfers WAL contents into the main database file

fixtures.text: In WAL mode recent commits are written to the -wal file first and are not yet in the main database file. A safe snapshot uses VACUUM INTO or the sqlite3_backup API. A checkpoint transfers the WAL contents back into the main database file.
I am not sure how SQLite handles this; I would have to check the documentation.
You can copy the database file at any time with cp; SQLite automatically keeps the file consistent, so no data is ever lost. There is no need for special tools.

expectation: Preregistered: delta approximately 0. Haiku knows SQLite WAL semantics cold; supplying archive context about contextd's own backup work should not materially change the score. This control exists so the harness demonstrably CAN return 'context barely matters' — if it shows a large positive delta here, suspect a scoring artifact or a prompt-wrapper effect before believing any positive result on the real task.
